contested.title: PNG reader in the backdrop e2e treats unknown filter types as Paeth and skips the full signature and CRC checks
contested.evidence: In `firstPixel`, the `else` branch applies Paeth to any filter byte other than 0 to 3, so a corrupt or unexpected value (5 or more) decodes quietly. Only bytes 1-3 ('PNG') of the 8-byte signature are checked, and a missing IHDR leaves width and channels at 0, so the reader returns [0,0,0] instead of failing. For Chromium's 1x1 clip every filter reduces to the raw byte, so today's results are correct. But the reader can return a value where it should fail loudly, which goes against the file's own fail-don't-pass stance.
contested.suggestion: Throw on a filter byte above 4, on a missing IHDR or empty IDAT, and on a raw length other than height*(stride+1). Optionally check the full 8-byte signature. Keep the 1x1 clip.
verifierNotes: Verified in e2e/nfr-14-backdrop.spec.ts firstPixel (lines ~115-155). The else branch applies Paeth to any filter byte other than 0-3, only bytes 1-3 of the signature are checked, and a missing IHDR with IDAT present returns [0,0,0] (no IDAT at all makes inflateSync throw). There is no raw-length check, and byteAt turns out-of-range reads into 0. All claims are accurate. The only caller, pixelAt, reads a Chromium screenshot of a 1x1 clip. For one pixel every filter reduces to the raw byte, and Chromium emits valid PNGs, so the lax paths are unreachable and results are correct today. This is a hardening nit with no real defect, and the finding's own minor severity and low confidence match that.

But the finding cannot occur for a real user or attacker. `firstPixel` is a private helper in a Playwright test. It only decodes PNGs from `page.screenshot` of a 1x1 clip, which Chromium produces itself, so no untrusted input reaches it. For a 1x1 image every filter type reduces to the raw byte, and Chromium never emits filter bytes above 4. No code path produces a malformed PNG, and the finding itself says today's results are correct. The only scenario is a hypothetical broken or changed screenshot encoder. In that case the read would most likely produce an implausible colour, and the case's pixel assertions would fail anyway. No attacker or user-facing impact exists, and the problem cannot be reproduced. This is a hardening nit about a test helper, not a reproducible defect.

contested.title: Hand-written PNG reader is correct for Playwright screenshots, but treats an unknown filter type as Paeth instead of failing
contested.evidence: I checked the reader: the chunk walk (offset += 12 + length), IHDR parsing, IDAT concatenation, inflateSync, bpp = channels for 8-bit, the Sub/Up/Average (floor) predictors and the Paeth predictor with the a, b, c tie order are all per the PNG spec. Colour types other than 2/6, other bit depths and interlace are refused loudly. However, the `else` branch handles every filter value other than 0-3 as Paeth, so a corrupt filter byte (>4) would decode silently. CRCs are not checked (acceptable). In practice the closed-pixel reads match the page colour in 10 of 10 cases and agree with the computed style in red, which supports the reader for this use.
contested.suggestion: Change the last branch to `else if (filter === 4)` and throw on any other filter byte. Optionally add a unit-level self-check that decodes a known tiny PNG.
